contributions.summary: A fitted tide boundary partitions exposure into no-contact, partial-submergence, and complete-submergence stages.
Airy-wave kinematics and a Morison inertia-drag relation produce a geometry-sensitive inline load.
A Mohr-Coulomb stress ratio is compared with a moisture-dependent internal-friction capacity.
Horton infiltration and a Van Genuchten retention curve update the moisture state during tide contact.
One cuboid walkthrough connects tide height, force, stress, moisture, friction angle, and a reported 50-minute collapse.
A six-shape equal-volume comparison and an aspect-ratio traversal turn the model chain into a bounded geometry decision.
An initial-moisture traversal keeps both the 5-percent duration maximum and the practical 15-percent recommendation visible.
Rainfall is split into drop kinematics, scour, and seepage before six rainy effective heights are compared.
ANSYS field plots provide a qualitative second computational representation before mechanism-linked practical advice.

results_trace.summary: The worked cuboid lasts about 40 minutes before contact and 10 minutes during partial submergence, for about 50 minutes total.
Table 1 selects the cuboid as the best of six under the dry tide-wave comparison.
The aspect-ratio plot supports making the water-facing width as narrow as practical.
The maximum plotted duration is 67 minutes at 5 percent initial water content.
The paper nevertheless recommends 15 percent initial water content and reports 64.43 minutes, citing stronger compactness and a small duration difference.
Rainy effective heights are 0.20, 0.15, 0.11, 0.08, 0.15, and 0.15 m, again selecting the cuboid.
ANSYS pressure, tension, and deformation fields are described as very similar to theory without a numerical agreement measure.
The Article translates the outputs into a cuboid, narrow water-facing side, strong-feeling wet sand near the 15-percent rationale, rain avoidance, and environmental cleanup advice.

weaknesses.summary: Equation (1) visibly prints 1256, but that coefficient is incompatible with Figure 2's centimeter-scale tide curve unless an omitted decimal point or unit transformation is documented; the source value must be retained rather than silently repaired.
The tide fit does not publish the underlying observations, fitting method, residuals, time unit, coefficient units, or datum conversion needed to reproduce the 40- and 50-minute readings.
Equations (3)-(4) treat time derivatives of free-surface elevation as wave-particle speed and acceleration without the depth-dependent Airy velocity field or a justification for that proxy.
The Airy-wave branch assigns amplitude, wavelength, and period but omits water depth, dispersion verification, vertical coordinate, near-shore transformation, attenuation, and phase calibration.
Equation (5) borrows Morison inertia and drag terms without checking Reynolds and Keulegan-Carpenter regimes, partial submergence, porous finite geometry, or shape-specific coefficient applicability.
Equations (7)-(8) use the same undivided total wave force to define normal and shear stresses, without resolving load direction or the components acting on a stated failure plane.
The reduction to zero cohesion in Equation (9) omits effective stress, pore pressure, saturation, and moisture-dependent cohesion even though the later failure calculation is driven by wetting.

Equation (11), g(w)=-140w^2+56w+28.5, does not reproduce Figure 4 under an explicit shared water-content scale; the plotted maximum and later percentage readings therefore lack a coherent calibration record.
With f_0=0 and f_c=1, Equation (12) increases toward f_c, contrary to the text's description of f_c as a minimum reached after saturation; parameter order, units, and calibration are unresolved.
The paper equates Van Genuchten pressure head psi with Horton infiltration rate f(t), although pressure head and rate have different physical dimensions and roles.

The reported 50-minute cuboid collapse lacks a published time grid, tide-to-depth conversion, submergence-dependent area, force, stress, water-content, friction-angle trace, interpolation rule, or executable calculation.

Table 1 reports coarse lasting times and effective heights for six shapes without complete dimensions, equal-volume verification, drag-coefficient assignments, intermediate calculations, uncertainty, or physical outcomes.
The aspect-ratio traversal provides neither bounds nor increments and yields only a narrower-front direction, not a feasible optimum robust to construction constraints or changing wave direction.

Figure 8 reports the longest duration, 67 minutes, at 5 percent initial water content, while the paper recommends 15 percent with 64.43 minutes; compactness is invoked without a formal decision criterion or experiment.

The paper alternates sand-to-water, water-to-sand, water-content, and initial-moisture language without freezing denominator, mass-versus-volume basis, preparation method, density, or compaction state.
Equation (14) does not fully state unit conversions, drop mass and density, branch continuity at 3 mm, or how one representative diameter stands for an event-level drop-size distribution.
Equation (15) gives d_50=2.52i^0.32, but Equation (16) substitutes i^0.23; the exponent conflict and transformed constants must be derived or corrected from source data before use.
The thresholds and constants in Equation (16) are not derived from Equations (14)-(15), and rainfall-intensity units, regression sample, fit error, and uncertainty are not supplied.

Equation (17), dP/dt=K_2Pr, has a positive sign while P is discussed as sand washed away or changing sand volume; P's state meaning, initial condition, integration, area conversion, and coefficient units are unresolved.

The seepage flowchart sends a raindrop-speed quantity into the Van Genuchten retention relation without a coupled rainfall-flux, pressure-head, conductivity, depth, boundary, or time-integration model.
Equation (18), phi=0.8462w+5.256, introduces a second moisture-friction fit without explaining its relation to Equation (11), its water-content scale, fit observations, residuals, or valid domain.

Table 2 gives six rain-conditioned effective heights without rainfall intensity, exposure duration, initial moisture, geometry ledger, failure definition, calculation trace, uncertainty, or observed comparator.
The ANSYS check omits version, project, geometry, units, mesh, material law, load magnitude, boundary conditions, solver settings, extraction procedure, and machine-readable results.
The statement that ANSYS and theory are 'very similar' is qualitative, has no common numerical metric, and is not an independent physical validation of either representation.

The claim that the model applies to beaches in any area exceeds a single Sandy Hook tide curve, fixed wave assumptions, uniform seepage approximation, selected sand parameters, and six-shape candidate set.

Shields, plastic wrapping, internal supports, stones, and clay extend beyond the no-additive mixture comparison and are not supported by durability, safety, cost, environmental, or field-effect experiments; the Article itself retains pollution and injury concerns.
